title: Japan's Nikkei falls over 3% as global chip selloff hits semiconductor stocks - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Japan’s Nikkei share average fell more than 3% on Tuesday, pressured by sharp declines in semiconductor-related stocks after weakness on Wall Street extended the global chip selloff. | Photo Credit: MANAMI YAMADA

Japan's Nikkei share average fell more than ​3% on Tuesday, dragged down by ‌heavy losses in chip-related stocks after their ​U.S. peers closed lower overnight.

The ⁠Nikkei was down 3.59% at 62,599.14 as of 0034 GMT, while the broader Topix ‌was lower 2.44% at 3,966.87.

"This is not a broad selloff, or ‌the market is not on ‌the risk-off ⁠sentiment," said Daisuke Hashizume, senior ⁠strategist at Daiwa Securities.

"Investors are cautious about buying stocks before earnings of big tech firms in ​the U.S. ‌and Japan. There are uncertainties in the market."

South Korea’s KOSPI falls over 7% as China chip threat hits SK Hynix, Samsung

Nvidia fell 4.9% overnight and the Philadelphia semiconductor index extended its recent ‌selloff, falling 2.2%. The index is ​down 21% from its record-high close on June 22, but up ⁠63% in 2026.

South Korea's benchmark KOSPI was down 7% in early trade on ‌Tuesday.

The Nikkei's moves have been heavily influenced by the tech-heavy KOSPI and the U.S. Philadelphia semiconductor index.

Chip-related Advantest and Tokyo Electron fell 7.52% and 8.84%, respectively.

Bank shares, which had ‌been rising on prospects of an early Bank ​of Japan interest rate hike, also fell, with Mitsubishi UFJ Financial ⁠Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group losing nearly ⁠3% each.

Of the more than 1,500 stocks trading on ‌the Tokyo Stock Exchange's prime market, 31% rose, 64% fell and 3% ​traded flat.
